title: Missing role guard in mahasiswa violation page causes unhandled HTTP 500 for administrators
description: The student violation page (`/pelanggaran`) is rendered after only redirecting away sessions whose `user_type` is `dosen`. It performs no role check for any other non-student role, then dereferences student-only session fields (`angkatan`, `nim`). An authenticated administrator reaching this route triggers a PHP undefined-array-key warning that the framework's error handler converts to an uncaught exception, returning **HTTP 500 Internal Server Error** instead of a controlled `403 Forbidden`.
impact: An authenticated administrator (or any authenticated session that is neither `mahasiswa` nor `dosen`) can force an unhandled server-side exception on a route they are not authorised to view. This is an availability and access-control-consistency defect: the page fails with a generic error rather than a deliberate denial, and the same class of bug was already remediated elsewhere (`/pelanggaran/dosen` returns `403` for administrators). The generic error page does not leak stack traces or internal paths, so confidentiality impact is limited; there is no state change or data exposure.
poc_description:
1. Authenticate as an administrator (`ADMIN002` / `admin456`) and retain the session cookie.
2. Request the student violation page: `GET /pelanggaran`.
3. Observe that the server responds with `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` and renders the generic "500 - Sistem Bermasalah" error page.
4. For contrast, request the lecturer page `GET /pelanggaran/dosen` with the same administrator session and observe a controlled `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`.
poc_script_code:
```python
import re
import requests

BASE = "http://172.17.112.1:8001"

s = requests.Session()
# 1. fetch login page + CSRF token
login_page = s.get(f"{BASE}/login").text
csrf = re.search(r'name="csrf_token" value="([^"]+)"', login_page).group(1)

# 2. authenticate as administrator
s.post(f"{BASE}/action/login", data={
    "csrf_token": csrf,
    "username": "ADMIN002",
    "password": "admin456",
    "user_type": "admin",
})

# 3. administrator requests the student-only violation page
r = s.get(f"{BASE}/pelanggaran")
print("GET /pelanggaran        ->", r.status_code)   # 500 (unhandled exception)

# 4. contrast: the guarded lecturer page denies correctly
r2 = s.get(f"{BASE}/pelanggaran/dosen")
print("GET /pelanggaran/dosen  ->", r2.status_code)  # 403 (fail-closed)
```
remediation_steps: Apply a fail-closed role guard to the student violation page. Immediately after the existing `dosen` redirect in `views/pelanggaran/pelanggaran-page.php`, abort with a controlled `403` when the session role is not `mahasiswa`, reusing the existing `app_abort_forbidden()` helper rather than falling through to student-only field access. More broadly, replace the ad-hoc per-view role checks with a single shared guard (e.g. `app_require_role('mahasiswa')`) invoked at the top of every role-scoped view and action handler, so that a request from an unexpected role always yields a deliberate denial instead of an unhandled exception.
evidence:
Administrator session against the student violation page:

```http
GET /pelanggaran HTTP/1.1
Host: 172.17.112.1:8001
Cookie: PHPSESSID=<admin session>

HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8

<title>500 - Sistem Bermasalah | DiscipLink</title>
```

Contrast — same administrator session, lecturer page denies in a controlled manner:

```http
GET /pelanggaran/dosen HTTP/1.1
Host: 172.17.112.1:8001
Cookie: PHPSESSID=<admin session>

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
```

Control — a `mahasiswa` session reaches the same page normally:

```http
GET /pelanggaran HTTP/1.1
Host: 172.17.112.1:8001
Cookie: PHPSESSID=<mahasiswa session>

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
assumptions: Requires an authenticated session whose `user_type` is neither `mahasiswa` nor `dosen` (e.g. `admin`). The impact is bounded to a controlled-denial failure (500 instead of 403) on one route; no data is exposed and no state is modified.

code_locations.label: Enforce student-only access with a fail-closed role guard

fix_pr_body:
## Summary

`GET /pelanggaran` (the student violation page) only redirects `dosen` sessions away and performs no guard for other roles. An administrator session therefore falls through to student-only session fields (`angkatan`, `nim`) that the `ADMIN` row does not contain, raising an undefined-array-key warning that the framework converts into an unhandled exception — returning `HTTP 500` instead of a controlled denial.

The sibling route `/pelanggaran/dosen` already returns `403` for administrators, so the intended behaviour for an out-of-role request is a fail-closed denial.

## Change

Add a fail-closed guard in `views/pelanggaran/pelanggaran-page.php` immediately after the existing `dosen` redirect: if the session role is not `mahasiswa`, abort with `403` (via the existing `app_abort_forbidden()` helper) rather than continuing to dereference student-only fields.

## Rationale

- Aligns the student page with the lecturer page's fail-closed behaviour.
- Converts an unhandled-exception `500` into a deliberate `403`.
- Deny-by-default for any role that is not explicitly permitted.
